messages.subject: smooth_check, LDSCoutput$S and LDSCoutput$V
parts:
Hi, 

I have two questions based on the message and 2 warnings I obtained: 

1. Where do I set "smooth_check = TRUE"? I want to later run a multivariate GWAS using parallel processing. 

2. Is the S matrix referred to in the message I get the LDSCoutput$S (the covariance matrix on the liability scale for case/control designs) or the LDSCoutput$V (the sampling covariance matrix in the format expected by lavaan)?

I added the LDSCoutput$S and LDSCoutput$V files as attachments. 

Thank you for your patience. I am a beginner! 

Camille 


CommonFactor_DWLS<- commonfactor(covstruc = LDSCoutput, estimation="DWLS") 
[1] "Running Model" 
[1] "Calculating CFI" elapsed 0.593 
 1] "The S matrix was smoothed prior to model estimation due to a non-positive definite matrix. The largest absolute difference in a cell between the smoothed and non-smoothed matrix was 0.0744047829376131 As a result of the smoothing, the largest Z-statistic change for the genetic covariances was 1.80833280592617 . We recommend setting the smooth_check argument to true if you are going to run a multivariate GWAS." 

Warning messages: 

1: In commonfactor(covstruc = LDSCoutput, estimation = "DWLS") : A difference greater than .025 was observed pre- and post-smoothing in the genetic covariance matrix. This reflects a large difference and results should be interpreted with caution!! This can often result from including low powered traits, and you might consider removing those traits from the model. If you are going to run a multivariate GWAS we strongly recommend setting the smooth_check argument to true to check smoothing for each SNP. 

2: In commonfactor(covstruc = LDSCoutput, estimation = "DWLS") : A difference greater than .025 was observed pre- and post-smoothing for Z-statistics in the genetic covariance matrix. This reflects a large difference and results should be interpreted with caution!! This can often result from including low powered traits, and you might consider removing those traits from the model. If you are going to run a multivariate GWAS we strongly recommend setting the smooth_check argument to true to check smoothing for each SNP.

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: smooth_check, LDSCoutput$S and LDSCoutput$V
parts:
Hi Camille, 

Good questions! Answers below:
1. I was actually behind on adding in the smooth_check argument so your post gave me the push to sit down and put that code in for the multivariate GWAS functions (userGWAS and commonfactorGWAS). Since I just updated that today you will want to reinstall Genomic SEM and restart R before running the multivariate GWAS, but you can now set smooth_check = TRUE within the context of either GWAS function. Since this functionality is new definitely let me know if you run into any issues or hard to make sense of error messages!

2. The S matrix refers to the genetic covariance matrix reflected in LDSCoutput$S. Smoothing of .07 at the level of the S matrix is fairly large and, as the warning you posted notes, you can certainly try and safeguard against false positives or negatives by setting smooth_check to TRUE and pruning out multivariate GWAS results that require a high degree of smoothing. However, you might also consider re-examining what traits you are choosing to include in the model as high levels of smoothing are typically a consequence of the more low powered traits. So if you have one particular trait among many that is low powered, you could try rerunning the model with that trait excluded and see how much smoothing still occurs. 

Best, 
  Andrew
